name: Solomon Islands SWIM
summary: SWIM (Supporting Work in Mission) is the CRCA's mission base in Honiara, Solomon Islands. It offers Bible teaching, leadership training, weekly community ministries, prison ministry and practical support, and hosts short-term mission teams.

hero.alt: A coastal road beside calm blue sea in the Solomon Islands, with a house on stilts at the water's edge and hills across the bay.

body.heading: What SWIM is
paragraphs: SWIM stands for Supporting Work in Mission. It is a mission arm of the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia (CRCA). In the Solomon Islands, SWIM is a Registered Charitable Trust and an associate member of the Solomon Islands Christian Association (SICA).

The Solomon Islands Workgroup (SIW) oversees SWIM for the CRCA, working with a local leadership team (LLT) and the base managers in Honiara. SIW board members visit the base to meet staff, check the facilities and see the ministries at work.

SWIM's main supporters are the members of CRCA churches in Australia, through their prayers, encouragement and giving. Churches and individuals have also sent containers of donated goods, run fundraising badges through Cadets and GEMS, and sent short-term mission teams.
SWIM works alongside churches across the Solomon Islands, and keeps up its links with SICA, the Solomon Islands Gospel Fellowship Association (SIGFA) and local congregations.

image.alt: SWIM staff and two visiting SIW board members standing together on the lawn in front of a base building in Honiara.
image.caption: SWIM staff with visiting board members, early 2026.

body.heading: Mission and vision
paragraphs: SWIM's mission: "Serving in Solomon Islands with compassion through Biblical teaching, equipping, and support in Jesus' name."

SWIM's vision: "As a mission community of Christ-centered people we will provide effective, practical, compassionate support and Bible based teaching and equipping ministries to build up Christians and establish self-reliant communities in Solomon Islands using our base facilities, resources, and the talents of our long and short term team members."

body.heading: Core biblical values
paragraphs: The Bible contains many values that shape decisions and inform ministry priorities. SWIM has chosen eight biblical values as the foundation of all its ministries. In SWIM's own words:
list: Biblical teaching: We value the Bible as God's authoritative and accurate word for salvation and service (2 Tim. 3:16-17; Deut. 4:19-14). Therefore, we will strive to teach God's Word with integrity and authority so those seeking will find Christ and believers will mature in him. We believe that the Bible is God's written revelation to humanity and the 66 books of the Bible given to us by the Holy Spirit are inspired equally in all parts (1 Cor. 2:7-14; 2 Peter 1:20-21).

Unity: We value unity focusing on the things that unite us, not the things that divide us. We are all united in our Lord Jesus Christ (Eph. 4:3-5; 1 Cor. 1:10). Refusing to give audience to a spirit of complaining, we will instead be courageous in solving every problem in a way that honours God and builds biblical character. We value healthy relationships by protecting the unity of the Spirit in our ministries (John 17:21; 1 Peter 3:8; Rom. 16:17; Psalm 133:1).

Teamwork: We value everyone and believe that "doing ministry as a team" is God's design for effective ministry (Ephesians 4:11-16; 1 Peter 2:4-9). A Spirit-empowered serving with the willing hearted involvement of every person is vital to God's plan being accomplished. We are stronger together than apart (1 Cor. 12:14-30; Eccl. 4:9-12).

Godly leadership: We value godly servant leadership and believe that a godly ministry can rise no higher than its leadership (2 Tim. 4:1-5; 1 Peter 5:1-4). It will be our goal to have men and women who possess servant leadership characteristics and can lead with godly wisdom, character, integrity, productivity, accountability and promote unity and biblical moral values (1 Cor. 3:5-23; Rom. 12:8).

Loving people: We value biblical community where people have opportunity to minister to and love one another. We believe no individual is ever more or less important than another (1 Cor. 13; 1 John 4:7-12). We also believe one of the main roles of our ministry is to serve and care for the poor, oppressed and marginalized in our villages, communities, and ministry contexts (Micah 6:8; 1 John 3:17; Matthew 25:31-46).

Prayer: We value prayer as a discipline that should precede and permeate our work. We believe that prayer should consume a significant part of our daily lives. Without prayer we are disconnected from God; our hearts and minds are at loose ends, doing what we think is right, instead of listening to God and doing what He says is right. Without prayer it is impossible to please God or succeed in ministry (Acts 2:42; Matthew 6:5-13; Eph. 6:18-20; 1 Tim. 2:1-4).

Spiritual growth: We value a commitment to consistent spiritual growth with honest accountability (2 Peter 1:5-9; Eph. 4:15-16). A genuine love for God is always the first priority. Every Christian should yearn for continual spiritual growth. Therefore, discipleship through small groups, accountability, and open honesty is critical to maturing in our faith (Mark 12:29-31; Acts 2:44-47; 1 Peter 2:2).

Cultural relevance: We believe that while God's message is timeless, forms and methods must adapt to those we are seeking to serve (1 Cor. 9:22; 2 Cor. 5:14-21). We believe it's important to speak the language of our culture while not compromising biblical truth. It is possible to guard the truth of the gospel and live holy lives while at the same time speaking and ministering in a manner which the culture we are trying to reach can understand (Luke 5:36-39).

body.heading: Weekly ministries at the base
paragraphs: Each week SWIM runs ministries for the neighbouring communities around the base. Every program includes a devotion, and numbers have grown steadily.

Women's ministry meets on Tuesdays for Bible study and life skills such as sewing, knitting, patching, tie-dyeing, cooking and baking. Visiting volunteers have run sewing courses, including a 5-day course in 2025 and a 3-day basic sewing course at Solmere Bethesda in 2024.

Children's ministry offers Bible stories, memory verses, singing, arts and crafts, face painting and drawing. In 2025 the teachers, Martina Gegeu, Janet Light and Phillistus Wate, completed training at the Evangelism School for Children and began a character-building program.
Youth ministry meets on Thursdays and is led by John Mark and Martina. It focuses on building Christlike character, with topics such as forgiveness, and ends the year with Bible quizzes.

Sports ministry starts with a devotion and then training. Young men from the nearby communities play in the SWIM FC futsal team, with Pastor Michael Light as head coach. SWIM FC played in the SALT 2024 Futsal Challenge and the Hatanga Futsal League in 2025, and about 50 young men came to the 2025 closing tournament.
In early 2025 the Solomon Islands Trauma Healing Association (SITHA) ran trauma healing sessions for the women's, children's and youth ministries.

image.alt: The SWIM FC futsal team in green uniforms, posing in two rows on an indoor court with their coaches.
image.caption: SWIM FC, the base's futsal team.

body.heading: Teaching and equipping church leaders
paragraphs: SWIM's pastor, Michael Light, runs biblical leadership training at the base and in the provinces. Courses bring together pastors, women's leaders and youth leaders from many churches, including SSEC, Assembly of God, Anglican and Church of Christ congregations. SWIM provides the teaching, resources and meals.

Recent courses include training for community church leaders at the base (February 2025), 20 pastors and leaders in Auki (April 2025), 29 community leaders in Samasodu (July 2025), more than 100 youths at the Zion Worship Centre in Malaita on end-time events (July 2025), more than 30 church leaders at Kwainafala (September 2025), more than 70 leaders at Baurara, East Fataleka (November 2025), and more than 60 leaders at Capernaum Centre, East Mbaelelea, North Malaita (January 2026). More than 20 leaders received certificates after a two-day course at Bethesda in Honiara.

Before Pastor Michael, Pastor Andrew Fanasia served as SWIM's pastor for four years. He and his wife Unity ran courses such as a five-day leadership training for the Marebo SSEC Association in November 2024, and a youth leadership course alongside grassroots futsal coaching for leaders from Lunga.
Know Your Bible (KYB) workshops have also been run in Honiara.

image.alt: A large group of men and women standing in front of a church building, holding up their training certificates.
image.caption: Leaders with their certificates after a SWIM leadership training, 2024.

body.heading: Crossroads prison ministry
paragraphs: Crossroad Bible Institute (CBI) equips the church to disciple people in prison with the Word of God, free of charge, wherever they are held. It is a personal, in-depth and long-term program that helps prisoners grow in a life-changing relationship with Jesus Christ, and prepares and helps them for a successful return to the community. Research shows a significant reduction in re-offending for people who receive Bible instruction while in prison.

Pastor Michael Light and his wife Janet coordinate the Crossroads ministry with SWIM. They teach weekly at Rove Correctional Centre in Honiara, where inmates work through courses such as "Great truths of the Bible" and "Survey of the Bible". More than 50 inmates graduated in late 2025, and in 2025 twenty students were recognised for good behaviour.

In 2026 the ministry grew to two more centres. More than 30 inmates graduated at Tetere Correctional Centre in February 2026, and SWIM trained 12 volunteers to teach Crossroads lessons at Auki Correctional Centre.
SWIM also gives release packs to inmates when they leave prison, and in December 2025 a SWIM team provided a Christmas meal at Rove Correctional Centre.

image.alt: A man standing outside the fenced entrance of Rove Central Correctional Centre in Honiara.
image.caption: Rove Central Correctional Centre, Honiara.

body.heading: Bethesda Disability Centre
paragraphs: Bethesda is being developed by SWIM together with the Ministry of Health and People With Disabilities Solomon Islands (PWDSI). It meets some of the needs of people with disabilities by teaching life skills and helping each person reach their full potential.

Construction began in April 2008. Since 2010 Bethesda has run three eight-week residential courses each year. Students learn about the Christian faith and personal healthcare, and gain skills such as gardening, woodwork and sewing, so they can be more self-sufficient in their communities.

The centre has student accommodation, an administration building and classrooms, ablution blocks and four staff houses. A poultry farm provides income to run the centre, and the long-term plan is for Bethesda to be fully self-sufficient from eggs and other produce grown on site. More staff houses are still needed, and building teams are welcome to help finish the project.

SWIM staff have also helped Bethesda in practical ways, such as building a laundry, and ran a pilot healthy eating and nutrition project with the centre in 2019. In 2024 Pastor Michael attended Bethesda's graduation for seven students, where Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele was the keynote speaker.

image.alt: Blue weatherboard buildings with louvred windows at the Bethesda Disability Centre, joined by a concrete path and garden beds.
image.caption: Bethesda Disability Centre.

body.heading: Samasodu village and Katova High School
paragraphs: SWIM partners in Australia, led from Wamberal CRC in New South Wales, have worked with Samasodu village in Isabel Province since 2006. Samasodu is about 22 hours by boat from Honiara. The first team of 27 volunteers built a medical clinic. Over the years teams built a Rural Health Centre and staff housing, and improved sanitation and the water supply.

The partnership is now building Katova High School for the Katova District. The plan includes about 50 buildings: classrooms, dormitories, kitchens, administration buildings and staff housing, so that more than 400 young people can go to high school. Rod Peet, an elder at Wamberal CRC, has coordinated the teams.

Teams have travelled most years since 2018, including 18 people in October 2018, 33 volunteers from Sydney, Tasmania and Perth in April 2019, a team in July 2024 that completed classrooms, toilets, staff houses and dormitories, and 35 people in July 2025 who built a new girls' dormitory, upgraded the school's wi-fi and helped teach. In 2024 SWIM also prepared a boat and engine for the school to use for transport.
Teams also run children's and community programs in the village, and SWIM's pastor ran the first biblical leadership training in Samasodu in 2025.

image.alt: Inside a timber classroom with long wooden desks, a dirt floor and colourful learning charts on the walls.
image.caption: A classroom in Samasodu.

body.heading: Community development and water projects
paragraphs: SWIM works with communities on practical projects that local people have asked for, often with help from short-term teams.

At Kwainafala in North Malaita, the community had struggled without a water supply for more than 50 years. In 2025 SWIM built a dam, two water tanks and 25 standpipes, giving 30 households access to clean water. SWIM also ran a three-day leadership training for the community's church leaders.

SWIM built the Honiara Hospital School more than ten years before 2019. It lets sick children and their brothers and sisters keep learning while in hospital, sometimes for months. In 2019 SWIM added a ramp from the children's ward, a toilet, water, lighting and ceiling fans, funded by more than $2,000 raised by Cadets and GEMS clubs in Australia and New Zealand.

Other projects have included disability toilets with the Community Based Rehabilitation program, a planned water tank, school repairs and toilets at Mamosa village, and building help for local churches and schools near the base.

body.heading: Practical aid and Days for Girls
paragraphs: SWIM gives practical help where it is needed. Containers of donated goods from Australia are cleared at the base and shared with the community. Donations have included knitted bonnets and socks for newborn babies at the hospital maternity ward, sterile aprons and exercise books for the Hospital School, and medical supplies for Honiara Hospital.
SWIM is part of the Days for Girls program, and gives release packs to people leaving prison.

image.alt: A woman smiling and holding up a clear bag containing a Days for Girls hygiene kit.
image.caption: Days for Girls.

body.heading: School sponsorship
paragraphs: The government education system in the Solomon Islands is under-resourced, and schooling is neither free nor compulsory. Many children do not go to school, and only a few go on to tertiary or university study.

SWIM has contact with many primary and secondary schools and helps children get an education as far as it can. Donations help pay tuition fees, school supplies and uniforms. There is never enough to pay fees for every child who needs help, so regular donors make a real difference. A one-off gift, such as a workplace collection, could also support a university student studying in your own field.

image.alt: A group of young people sitting and standing on the steps of a green timber building.
image.caption: Students supported through school sponsorship.

body.heading: Short-term mission teams
paragraphs: There is nothing short about God's call to mission. However long people are physically in the country, all of SWIM's mission is long-term mission. Teams from Australia, New Zealand and elsewhere travel to the Solomon Islands to take part in God's mission through SWIM, and SWIM provides training resources for every team.

Over the years dozens of teams have come to the SWIM base. A trip might last several weeks or longer, and sometimes individuals come to join SWIM's work. What does it mean to serve in the Solomon Islands? Is it service, tourism, a personal pilgrimage or something else? These trips can affect people culturally and challenge them to think about their own faith.

SWIM is committed to resourcing everyone who comes to serve, so that short-term mission supports the long-term mission, is culturally relevant, and works towards self-reliant communities in the Solomon Islands. Building or trade skills are very useful, but a willing heart to serve matters most.

body.heading: Conduct and dress code for teams
paragraphs: All team members sign the SWIM short-term mission agreement form. While part of a team in the Solomon Islands, everyone agrees to:
list: No alcohol, betel nut, illicit drugs or smoking (including cigarettes) at any time.
No coarse or crude language, swearing or blasphemy.
Wear modest clothing that follows the SWIM dress code.
Respect culturally appropriate ways of relating to the opposite sex. In general, no physical contact apart from shaking hands, with other team members or with Solomon Islanders.

Women: loose shorts or skirts over the knee (some villages require skirts only, so check with your SWIM contact), a dress or skirt and a top covering the shoulders for church, loose and modest tops with wide shoulder straps, and board shorts with a T-shirt for swimming.
Men: loose shorts or board shorts for swimming, ideally with a T-shirt or singlet.
Everyone: no clothing with offensive pictures or words, light cotton clothes, thongs and a spare pair, strong sandals for muddy tracks, and a hat.
The dress code is deliberately conservative so that teams are above reproach. It also gives the best sun protection and comfort. You don't need a new wardrobe: borrow or visit a second-hand shop.

body.heading: Full-time roles
paragraphs: From time to time the SIW recruits long-term mission workers for the base. The Deed Missionary looks after all SWIM buildings and property, supervises new building work, maintains SWIM's vehicles and equipment, and prepares and orders supplies for SWIM team projects, working alongside the other base staff.

Packages for long-term workers are agreed with the SIW Board and can include on-base accommodation, use of a vehicle, superannuation, insurance and travel. To ask whether any role is currently open, contact the SIW Chairperson.

body.heading: The base
paragraphs: The SWIM base is on a 5 acre block on the eastern outskirts of Honiara, about 12 km from the town centre and 4 km from the international airport. Drinking water comes from rain catchment and other water from a bore. The houses have 240V power from solar panels, backed up by a generator. A new solar system was installed in late 2025 to cut fuel use, and new solar lighting in early 2026.
Long-term team members live and do much of their daily work in seven houses on the base. Staff keep the grounds, gardens and buildings in good order, and grow vegetables in the base garden.

image.alt: A long yellow building with a green roof set among lawns and large shade trees at the SWIM base in Honiara.
image.caption: The SWIM base, Honiara.

body.heading: Conference centre and accommodation
paragraphs: The Conference Centre and Transit House sleeps 34 people in bunk-style rooms. A large central area holds the common room, dining area and kitchen.

A large leaf meeting house is available for conferences and workshops, with extra facilities. There are plenty of quiet spaces for small groups, grass and garden areas for recreation, and the beach is a 20 minute walk away.

The centre is available for short-term mission teams, retreats, conferences and workshops. Rates are very reasonable and self-catering is usually required, although SWIM also offers catering. Recent guests include church and youth groups, government ministries, university groups, community organisations and Bible college students. Contact SWIM for bookings, rates or questions.

items.title: Contact the SWIM Directors
items.text: Mission opportunities are those identified by SWIM's long-term missionaries. Talk with the SWIM Directors first and keep in touch with them while you plan.

items.title: Form your team
items.text: Teams should have no more than 10 people. Larger teams need permission from the SWIM Directors. Team leaders must be confessing Christians active in their local church, with a reference letter from their pastor.

items.title: Sign the agreement form
items.text: Every team leader and member signs the SWIM short-term mission agreement form, committing to SWIM's Christian values and principles.

items.title: Complete training before you go
items.text: All team members complete short-term mission training and orientation before the trip. SWIM provides training resources and recommends the 'Helping without Hurting in Short Term Missions' video study.

items.title: Serve alongside SWIM
items.text: Where possible, a SWIM missionary or staff member goes with the team. Teams follow the policy on conduct and dress, including no alcohol, betel nut or smoking.

news.title: Newsletter: January to March 2026
news.summary: Board members visit, leadership training in North Malaita and at Bethesda, and the Crossroads prison ministry grows to Tetere and Auki.
paragraphs: We give thanks to almighty God for his guidance, protection and provision through the 2025 Christmas holidays. As we enter 2026, we continue to pray for God's guidance and protection over our staff and their daily work. We appreciate the SIW and LLT leaders for their continuing leadership and support, and look forward to working together in mission and in supporting Christian work in our communities and the Solomon Islands.
New staff: we welcome our new security officer, Chris Talo, from Guadalcanal Province. Chris also plays in the SWIM FC team.

Visitors: two board members from Australia, Michael and Daniel, visited the base from 28 January to 4 February. Pastor Michael encouraged the staff in their devotion on Joshua 3:3-17, with the theme "taking a leap of faith".

Weekly devotion: the weekly staff devotion helps staff grow in their spiritual life. Pastor Michael Light spoke on Philippians 4:13, "I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me", and on John 15:5, "I am the vine; you are the branches."

Biblical leadership training: a three-day course was held from 22 to 25 January at Capernaum Centre, East Mbaelelea, North Malaita, for more than 60 leaders. A two-day course at Bethesda in Honiara ended with more than 20 leaders receiving a certificate of attainment.

SWIM ministries: the sports ministry began the year with devotion and training. Hellen shared from Psalm 119:11 with the women's ministry, which started the year with devotion and activity planning with base manager Karin.

Crossroads prison ministry: the ministry has grown into the provinces. We trained 12 volunteers to teach Crossroads Bible study lessons at Auki Correctional Centre. On Monday 2 February, more than 30 inmates at Tetere Correctional Centre graduated from "Great truths of the Bible" and "Survey of the Bible". On 23 December 2025 a SWIM team provided a Christmas meal at Rove Correctional Centre.

Bookings: guests this quarter included the West AreAre Rokotanikeni Association (WARA) for its first management retreat of 2026, HOPE Trust for its planning day (they thanked us for the food and the workshop setting), Live and Learn for five days of training for rangers from four communities in Marau, and students from Global Mission Bible Institute for a day retreat.

Base work: staff weeded the vegetable garden, which saves buying vegetables at the market, installed new clotheslines, repainted House 8, cleared dry branches, laid gravel on the base road and kept the grounds and Transit House clean. We thank God for new solar lighting, which helps security and reduces fuel costs. We also wished Karin a happy 65th birthday.

Praise points: God's provision, faithfulness and goodness in 2026; financial support from the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia; SWIM's ministries as a helping hand to the surrounding community; and open doors for Crossroads at Tetere and Auki.

Prayer points: SWIM's operation plan for 2026; SWIM staff and families; new ministry opportunities, including feeding the hungry at the dump site; and our partners in the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia.
With grateful hearts we thank every SWIM staff member for their contribution over the past three months.

news.title: Newsletter: October to December 2025
news.summary: Clean water for Kwainafala, leadership training in Malaita, end-of-year ministry celebrations and a new solar system for the base.
paragraphs: We give thanks to God for his provision throughout 2025, and appreciate our SIW and LLT leaders for their leadership in another year of mission and Christian work in our communities and the Solomon Islands.
New staff: we welcome Eunice Menapi, our new administration assistant and PR worker. Eunice is married and comes from Temotu.

Testimonies: Margret from the women's ministry thanked God for Tuesdays at SWIM, where she learns the word of God and sewing skills to share with her community. Winnie from the youth ministry said her parents noticed her changed attitude after lessons on building godly character, such as forgiveness. Bobby Kala of Kwainafala said: "For more than 50 years our community Kwainafala have struggled with no water for our daily basic necessities. We thank God that through the SWIM water project that has provided us with building a dam, 2 water tanks and 25 standpipes, we can now have access to clean water." Pastor George from Fouia, East Malaita, said the training on end-time prophecies had blessed leaders serving in remote communities.

Leadership training: more than 70 pastors, women and youth leaders completed a three-day course on end-time prophecies at Baurara, East Fataleka, from 21 to 23 November. The sessions were held in the open air. At Kwainafala, more than 30 church leaders took part in a three-day course from 13 to 15 September, alongside the water project.

Kwainafala water project: 30 households in North Malaita now benefit from a SWIM water project. The community had faced great difficulty getting water, and they see the finished project as an answer to prayer.

Ministries: all the ministries ended the year with celebrations. About 20 women enjoyed songs, dancing and a secret sister gift exchange. Around 40 children shared their memory verses in song and action and received lunch boxes. The sports ministry finished with its championship final, attended by 50 young men. The youth ministry ended with Bible quizzes and water bottles as Christmas gifts.
New solar system: we praise God for a new solar system at the base, which reduces our use of fossil fuel.
Crossroads: more than 50 inmates graduated with certificates in "Great truths of the Bible" in October and "Bible survey" in November. Photos are not available for security reasons.
Praise points: God's goodness and faithfulness in 2025, his provision and blessing, the many lives blessed through SWIM, and the teamwork and unity of the year.

Prayer points: God's direction and provision for SWIM in 2026; wisdom, strength and courage for the SIW and LLT; the Christian Reformed Churches of Australia; SWIM's plans, training and ministries for 2026; more open doors to reach the Solomon Islands with the gospel; and the health and needs of SWIM staff and their families.

Christmas greetings came from Pastor Michael Light and from base managers Joh and Karin Van Straten. "And do not forget to do good and to share with others, for with such sacrifices God is pleased." (Hebrews 13:16)

news.title: Newsletter: July to September 2025
news.summary: A new girls' dormitory at Katova High School, training in Auki and Samasodu, and release packs for prisoners.
paragraphs: Almighty Father, we come again to give glory and honour for your continued guidance, protection and love. We lift up your teaching through the outreach, ministries and programs SWIM offers to communities in Honiara, the provinces and overseas.

Testimonies: Kevin Jack, a SWIM FC winger, said he had been looked down on because of his appearance, but at SWIM FC he felt welcomed, valued and accepted. "God created each of us to be unique for a reason. Be yourself, love yourself."

Base manager Karin Van Straten presented a release pack to a man pardoned from a life sentence and released on 26 June 2025. The Commandant thanked SWIM for its continued support for the rehabilitation of inmates at Rove Correctional Centre.

Mrs Margret Maefiti, vice-president of the Samasodu Clinic Committee, said she was grateful to be part of the first biblical training in Samasodu. Catechist Sina said the training would affect her life and her Sunday school students, and that this kind of training is much needed in rural areas.

Leadership training: in July 2025, 29 community leaders in Samasodu took part in a two-day biblical leadership course. Later that month more than 100 youths from Malaita Province met at the Zion Worship Centre for training on end-time events, and newly baptised youths received new Bibles from SWIM.

Katova project, Samasodu: a 35-member team served at Katova Community High School. The advance team arrived on 1 July for logistics and the main team on 6 July. Over two weeks they built a new dormitory, upgraded the school's wi-fi and helped teach students, leaving on 20 July. "It was more than just work, it was ministry."
Ministries: our weekly women's, children's, youth and SWIM FC ministries keep growing in numbers, worship and praise.

Repairs and maintenance: repairs continued on House 4 and the Deed House, including a broken tank. We thank God for our groundsman and staff who keep the base well cared for. "Whatever you do, work at it with all your heart, as working for the Lord, not for human masters." (Colossians 3:23)
Praise points: God's faithfulness over the past six months, the many lives blessed through SWIM over the years, and the completion of the new girls' dormitory at Katova High School.

Prayer points: God's leading and provision for the rest of 2025; our ministries to children, youth, sport, women, prisoners and leaders; and the Kwainafala water project in North Malaita, especially the safe handling of materials and the work planned for October 2025.
Thank you to everyone who has given, sent materials or helped SWIM in any way, and to the SIW, LLT and the SWIM staff and management.

news.title: Newsletter: April to June 2025
news.summary: Training for pastors in Auki, a board visit, a sewing course, a container of donations and a busy season of bookings.
paragraphs: Time flies when you are seeing God's work unfold. As we start a new quarter, we are glad to share the workshops, ministries and activities at the SWIM base. All glory to the Almighty for guiding our mission.

New security officer: we welcome Mr Mattew Tarai, from West 'Are'are in Malaita Province. He and his wife Hellen Hikimae Tarai have six children and three grandchildren. "I have been staying at the Plywood community and have seen the support that SWIM has done for us. I look forward to working to keep the SWIM base safe."

Auki leadership training: from 1 to 3 April, 20 pastors and leaders from SSEC, AOG, Anglican and COC churches met for worship, learning and fellowship. They thanked SWIM and Pastor Michael Light for the biblical training, resources and meals.

Board visit: SWIM board members Mike Vos and Daniel van Rensburg made an official visit. They interviewed staff, inspected the facilities, visited Bethesda Disability Care Centre, and finished at Rove Correctional Centre, where they saw the effect of the Crossroads ministry.
Sewing team: SWIM's 5-day sewing course ended with celebration. We are grateful to Jan, Ingeborg, Ella, Lois, Jola and Rose.
Container arrival: after weeks of preparation and paperwork, a container arrived safely at the base. Thanks to Ingeborg, who oversaw the distribution of its contents, and to all our generous donors.
Bookings: May and June were among our busiest months, with catering, accommodation and venue hire for workshops and celebrations. Everything ran smoothly.

Maintenance and repairs: the water pump and bore for the Admin House were completed, House 8 is nearly finished with a new kitchen sink, and the leaf hut conference area was repaired. Staff are planting flowers and preparing a vegetable garden.

SWIM FC is playing in the Hatanga Futsal League, with 3 wins and 4 losses so far. The women's ministry is learning sewing and studying strong women of the Bible such as Esther and Deborah. Children's teachers Martina Gegeu, Janet Light and Phillistus Wate completed training at the Evangelism School for Children and began a character-building phase. The youth ministry, led by John and Martina, is focusing on Christlike character.

Testimonies from Crossroads at Rove Correctional Centre: "I thought God couldn't love someone like me. But now I understand grace, and I want to live a new life with faith." Another student said, "I felt ashamed and lost. But through the Crossroad study, my eyes were opened. I'm no longer ashamed. I'm blessed and happy."

Praise points: God's grace on SWIM in the first half of the year; the Crossroads ministry, where 20 students were recognised for good behaviour; and a stable workforce, steady guests and the weekly ministries.

Prayer points: the leaders of the Solomon Islands, Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele and his government, and Governor General Sir David Tiva Kapu; SWIM's plans for the next six months; the new dormitory and 70 new students at Katova High School; and shipping materials for the Kwainafala water project.
A heartfelt thank you to the SWIM team, the board, base managers, LLT and all staff, and to our major supporters, the members of the CRC churches in Australia.

news.title: Newsletter: January to March 2025
news.summary: New base managers and a new head builder arrive, trauma healing sessions for the ministries, and Crossroads release packs.
paragraphs: Heavenly Father, we come before you with hearts full of gratitude and joy for your protection, guidance and love through 2024 and into 2025.

New head builder: as SWIM opened for 2025 we welcomed Mr John Mark from North Malaita, who is married to Martina Gegeu. "I am so privileged and honoured to be part of a ministry as SWIM that involves our neighbouring communities and whose core foundation is helping others through mission and worship." SWIM opened the year with a staff devotion.
Leadership training: Pastor Michael Light ran leadership training for community church leaders on 15 and 22 February, with the theme "Empowering to lead".

New base managers: Johannes and Karin Van Straten arrived safely on 28 February with their dog Loba. "I am very happy to be here, feel very welcomed and this is a beautiful place with beautiful people," said Karin.

SWIM ministries: the Solomon Islands Trauma Healing Association (SITHA) ran a three-part course for the women's, children's and youth ministries, helping children and young people deal with trauma and stress at home, at school and among friends.

Crossroads: inmates are studying "The great truths of the Bible" and "Who is Jesus". The ministry also provides release packs, and inmates were moved to tears by them. "I am thankful and humbled to be given this gift. It is just what I would need to start my life outside prison." Pastor Michael and Janet Light teach at the correctional centre every Tuesday.

Testimonies: Nelly Tabe, a teenager from Agape Community opposite the base, said the trauma healing session helped her understand herself, respect herself and others, and seek God first. Alick Mau, 13, has come to SWIM's children's ministry since he was five and now joins the youth ministry: "SWIM have taught me a lot about the Bible, how to be brave in public and how to be kind." Pastor John Tolossi of New Light Ministry, Assembly of God, Gilbert Camp, said the two-day leadership workshop strengthened his faith and that he would take the training back to his church.
Praise points: changed lives through the Crossroads Bible study program; the safe arrival of Joh and Karin; and great team spirit among the 2025 staff.

Prayer points: SWIM's links with SICA, SIGFA and the churches of the Solomon Islands; the Katova High School and Kwainafala water projects as they near completion; and the leadership training planned for 1 to 3 April in Auki, Malaita.
A big thank you to everyone who helps SWIM Solomon Islands through prayer, thanksgiving, help and love. Tagio tumas, and may God bless you all.

news.title: Final newsletter for 2024
news.summary: Leadership and futsal workshops, Bethesda's graduation, SWIM FC's first season, and farewell to Pastor Andrew Fanasia.
paragraphs: All glory to the Almighty for keeping us safe and healthy as we come to the end of another year. As we close the year we look back on SWIM's work with other communities, from water projects to leadership training. God is good. May your festive season be blessed.

Leadership and futsal workshop: youth and community leaders from Lunga took part in a youth leadership course and grassroots futsal coaching. The coaching was run by Futsal Development Officer Mr Dickson Kadau and the leadership program by SWIM's Pastor Andrew Fanasia.

Marebo leadership training: Pastor Andrew and Unity Fanasia ran a five-day course for leaders of the Marebo SSEC Association from 11 to 15 November, helping community leaders to "lead with a difference" according to the Bible.
Women's ministry: the women began a three-day basic sewing course at Solmere Bethesda.
Bethesda graduation: Pastor Michael attended Bethesda's graduation for seven students. The keynote speaker, Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele, told the graduates, "You are blessed, you are unique."

SWIM FC: our young men's group competed in the SALT 2024 Futsal Challenge. All were new to the game, and with Pastor Michael Light as head coach they gave an excellent effort and plan to train hard for next year.
Ministry closings: the women's ministry closed on 26 November, the children's ministry on 27 November and the young men's ministry on 5 December, each with gifts, food and treats.

Staff closing: on 6 December SWIM management thanked staff for their hard work and farewelled Pastor Andrew Fanasia and head builder Mr Norman Kafula. Pastor Andrew thanked SWIM management, the LLT and SIW members for his four years as SWIM's pastor. "I will be here for any future consultation or any leadership program SWIM would like to do. I am always ready to help."

Prayer points: that SWIM's work will be a light to communities across the Solomon Islands; for Pastor Andrew Fanasia and family; for our new pastor, Pastor Michael Light, and family; for everyone at SWIM, the SIW, LLT and board members; for our projects in 2025; and for the SWIM staff and management.

news.title: SWIM news: third quarter 2024
news.summary: Welcoming Pastor Michael and Janet Light, a busy season of bookings, the Katova High School team, and visits to the Prime Minister and Governor General.
paragraphs: SWIM Solomon Islands is happy to share another three months of ministry as we pass the halfway point of the year. As you read, we invite you to reflect on the values SWIM stands for in your own life, and to do what you can for God's kingdom. "For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast. For we are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand that we should walk in them." (Ephesians 2:8-10)

Welcoming Pastor Michael Light: the SWIM base welcomes our new assistant pastor, Michael Light. He is from Uka'ai village in North Malaita and is married to Janet. They have one daughter and two grandchildren. "I am very excited to be part of a mission base with a great vision, a great working team and an even greater mission to achieve."

Their story: mission was already part of Michael and Janet's life when COVID-19 hit. They were serving with Hope Mission in Fiji and had to return home to the Solomon Islands. In February 2024 they chose the SWIM base for a weekend away. As they drove out they met Pastor Andrew Fanasia and asked about the assistant pastor role. Michael applied, was interviewed and joined the team. "It was God's timing and God's appointment."

SWIM ministries: our ministries keep growing week by week, and each program includes a devotion. Children enjoy arts and crafts, face painting, drawing and singing. The women's ministry includes Bible sharing, cooking, baking, knitting, patching and tie-dyeing. The young men's ministry focuses on soccer skills and games.

Busy months: June, July and August were busy, with seminars, workshops and stopovers for teams heading to the provinces. We hosted local youth, fellowship groups, government ministries and a university group.

Katova High School: a boat and engine were bought in Honiara for the school in Samasodu. The SWIM team fitted seats and the school logo, tested it on the Lunga River, and Dudley and the team then took it to Samasodu. The advance team, Machi, Jack, John and Trent, arrived on 1 July to arrange the ship, containers, machinery and fuel. Machi came a week earlier to run a KYB workshop at All Saints Hall and met the prison program officer to start lessons for inmates.

The main team, led by Rod Peet, arrived on 7 July, rested briefly at the base and then sailed for Isabel. They returned on 20 July after a rough crossing and flew back to Brisbane on 21 July. The team completed classrooms, toilets, staff houses and dormitories, and the school is expected to open soon.

Farewells and welcomes: SWIM farewelled two staff members and their families with a gathering in the leaf hut conference house, speeches and a token of thanks. A separate welcome was held for Pastor Michael and Janet Light. As usual in the Solomons, there was cake and a feast.

Gifts to the hospital: the container that arrived last quarter also held knitted bonnets for babies, sterile aprons and exercise books. Pastor Andrew and Maria delivered them to the Hospital School and gave bonnets and socks to newborn babies in the maternity ward. The nurse in charge thanked the donors.

Prime Minister and Governor General: Pastor Andrew, Unity and Maria visited the Prime Minister's Office, shared a message with the staff and gave Prime Minister Jeremiah Manele a leadership Bible. On 21 August Pastor Andrew and Unity, with Pastor Michael and Janet, visited the new Governor General, Reverend David Tiva Kapu, and Madam Salome Kapu, prayed for them and gave them a leadership Bible. Sir David asked them to pray for God's wisdom so he could lead with fairness and honesty.
Praise points: God's guidance, love and protection; growing numbers in SWIM's local ministries; and Pastor Michael Light and his family as he takes on the Word ministry.

Prayer points: the national government, the Prime Minister's Office, the Governor General and his family; SWIM staff who have moved to other work; and the Katova School project, its opening and its influence in Isabel Province and beyond.

news.title: Pirini Ponders: August 2019
news.summary: A healthy eating project, staff health checks, literacy in the children's ministry and the finished hospital school extensions.
paragraphs: Greetings to you all. We have had a busy couple of months with visits from friends and family, which has been a real blessing. Our daughter Charlotte visited for a couple of weeks and we spent a weekend camping Solomons style, with snorkelling, swimming and an early mountain climb to see the sunrise.

The healthy eating and nutrition project has been a great success this month and well received by SWIM staff and families. Emma, from Kingston church in Tasmania, stayed for three weeks. She wrote up log charts, trialled healthy recipes and cooked with Betty. She also helped design and build an outside oven with a chimney and bamboo pipe that takes smoke out of the cooking hut.

Charlotte's nursing skills helped with staff health checks: glucose, urine, weight and BMI measurements, blood pressure and a questionnaire on eating and exercise. Staff rotated through the stations and finished with morning tea and cake, followed by a talk on healthy diets and lifestyle.

The Wednesday evening children's ministry has started again, with a focus on teaching literacy using phonics, actions and alphabet signs for the deaf. Some adults who cannot read are also taking part, and more than 50 people came on the first night. Thanks to Ana, one of our SWIM family, for leading this.
The hospital school extensions are complete and look amazing. Ron and the building team attended the official opening and lunch.
Otherwise it has been business as usual, with a busy July school holidays hosting several teams and ongoing maintenance of the base. Please feel free to drop us a line with your news.
All our love and God's blessings, Ron and Tanya

news.title: Pirini Ponders: June 2019
news.summary: A healthy eating project with Bethesda, a water need at Mamosa village, and a ramp and toilet for the hospital school.
paragraphs: Greetings again from the Solomon Islands. We are thankful for a couple of weeks' leave in New Zealand and Fiji, including the engagement of our daughter Charlotte to Ben Starr and time with our granddaughter Lily. We are grateful that the base ran smoothly in our absence, thanks to our staff's hard work.

We are working with Bethesda Disability Centre on a healthy eating and nutrition pilot. Once the materials, model gardens and kitchens are ready, we will train SWIM and Bethesda staff and families, and later the wider community, in what a healthy plate looks like.

We visited Mamosa village, about 90 minutes' drive from the base. We found a need for a water tank, classroom repairs and community toilets. The village collects all its water from a spring into a container. The plan is to dam the spring and pipe water to a tank so there is a constant supply. If you have a team looking for a mission trip, let us know.

Our staff are building a ramp and an inside toilet at the hospital school, a long-overdue need. Students who are patients will be able to reach the classroom from the hospital and have a bathroom to use.
Otherwise it has been general repairs and maintenance, and helping our local church with building work and an upcoming convention.
Prayer: thanks for a refreshing holiday; for our families at home; and for the SIW board as it plans and recruits staff for the base after a recent review.
All our love and God's blessings, Ron and Tanya

news.title: Pirini Ponders: April 2019
news.summary: Election unrest in Honiara, a shower block at Su'u school, and a team of 33 building Katova High School.
paragraphs: Greetings from the Solomon Islands. Elections were the main topic of conversation, and on Wednesday 24 April there was rioting and unrest after the new Prime Minister was announced. The police were prepared and prevented major damage, with two nights of curfew and a liquor ban. The base is on the outskirts of town, so we felt safe and stayed put.

During this time we hosted two returning teams. Bethlehem College from Tauranga built a girls' shower block and a working toilet block at Su'u school in Malaita, something the school had not had in 15 years. Teachers said students cried when they saw water coming from the shower block.

At the same time, 33 CRCA volunteers from Sydney, Tasmania and Perth continued serving the Katova community, building a high school for the Katova District in Isabel Province. The project includes 50 buildings: classrooms, dormitories, kitchens, administration and staff housing. More than 400 young people will get the chance to go to high school. The team also ran a children's program.
We are proud of our staff, who worked hard through the elections and riots and took on extra work when the base hosted three teams at short notice.

We continue to help with building projects at the local church and school. Once our container arrives we will start work at the Honiara Hospital School: a new toilet and ramp for children in hospital and their families, funded by CRCA Cadets and GEMS. Thank you to these children for their generosity. We are also building disability toilets with the Community Based Rehabilitation program.

A village project is likely to go ahead in October, with interest from a small team in Nelson, New Zealand. Other small church groups considering a mission trip are welcome to contact us. A building or trade background is ideal, but God can use a willing heart.

Prayer: for the base and staff amid possible unrest; for our families at home; for the CRCA, the board and committees deciding SWIM's future direction after a recent review; and for safe travel on our break in New Zealand.
All our love and God's blessings, Ron and Tanya

news.title: February 2019 newsletter: the Honiara Hospital School
news.summary: A spotlight on the Honiara Hospital School, built by SWIM, and the Cadets and GEMS fundraising for its improvements.
paragraphs: Greetings from SWIM. A new year has begun, and we pray that God would lead us and give us wisdom as we serve our King and his people in the Solomon Islands and at home.

This newsletter puts the spotlight on the Honiara Hospital School. It is at Honiara Hospital, the main referral hospital in the Solomon Islands. Sick children and their brothers and sisters can continue, or sometimes begin, their education while in hospital. Hospital stays can last months, and families from other islands often have no other way to keep their children learning.

SWIM built the Hospital School more than ten years ago. It has been run by local people, including the current teacher, Betty. During a visit earlier this year, the teacher and the head paediatrician identified needed improvements: ceiling fans and lighting, an access ramp from the children's ward, a water supply and a toilet.

SWIM partnered with GEMS and Cadets to raise funds. Australian clubs completed their mission badge for the Hospital School in 2018, and New Zealand clubs began in 2019. More than $2,000 has been raised so far. Boys and girls also wrote encouragement cards for the children at the school. Tangio tumas (thank you very much).

Prayer: for SWIM missionaries and staff in the new year; for the Hospital School, its students and their generous teacher; for the planning and building of the improvements; and for SWIM and the SIW during the review of SWIM's future direction.
"Oh, taste and see that the LORD is good. Blessed is the man who takes refuge in him." (Psalm 34:8)

news.title: Pirini Ponders: February 2019
news.summary: Flooding, a damaged truck, a CRCA review, school sponsorship and a visit from the Crossroads coordinator.
paragraphs: Happy new year and greetings to you all. We came back to the base in early January after flooding over the new year. There was no major damage on the base, but the roads are terrible, so trips to town are back to 45 bumpy minutes.

Our Canter truck needed major repairs after taking in water. It will be off the base for another six weeks waiting for parts from Australia. The truck is SWIM's lifeline for everyday tasks and for visiting teams.
We started the year with a visit from a CRCA representative reviewing the SWIM base and meeting with locals.

School sponsorship for 2019 is in full swing. It is exciting to see students eager to learn. There is never enough money to pay fees for every child, but thanks to regular donors we have been able to cover almost all of them. If you would like to help, let us know. A one-off donation, such as a workplace collection, could support a university student studying in your line of work.

The Crossroads Prison Ministry coordinator visited and spent time with our prison ministry worker. This helped him understand the work here, and new practices were put in place to improve teaching and support for inmates on release.

Ron visited a traditional village with no water tanks or shared bathrooms, where the classroom roof leaks and damages teachers' resources. If your church has a team considering a mission trip, this could be a project for you.

Elections are the main topic of conversation, and extra police from New Zealand and Australia have arrived. We are praying for peace. We have started attending a church closer to the base and look forward to helping with it and its school. Our daughter Elise is doing well, and we thank everyone for their prayers.
Prayer: for SWIM staff in the new year; for our families at home; for the CRCA, the board and committees deciding SWIM's future direction; and for the elections.
All our love and God's blessings, Ron and Tanya

news.title: September 2018 newsletter: Katova High School project
news.summary: A team of 18 prepares to start work on Katova High School in Samasodu, continuing a partnership that began in 2006.
paragraphs: Greetings from SWIM. God's work never stops, and so it is with his work in the Solomon Islands. Work on the base continues, from preaching at workshops and open-air rallies to fixing cars, cleaning sheets and mowing lawns. A huge thank you to all the team who support God's mission through their work at SWIM.

This newsletter focuses on the Katova High School project in Samasodu, a village about 22 hours by boat from Honiara. The partnership between Samasodu and Wamberal CRC in New South Wales began more than ten years ago. In 2006 a team of 27 volunteers built a much-needed medical clinic. Nine trips and more than 220 participants later, relationships have grown and construction of a high school will soon begin.

A team of 18, coordinated by Rod Peet, an elder at Wamberal CRC, will travel from Thursday 18 October to Thursday 1 November 2018. The work includes a ministry program, a school program, catering, water supply, earthmoving, surveying, and setting up a workshop and timber mill.

A special collection was held for the project in Australian reformed churches earlier this year, and the team has almost reached its budget. Thank you for your gifts and prayers. A short video, "Katova High School Building Project", is on YouTube. Another trip is planned for April 2019.

Prayer: for SWIM missionaries and staff at the end of a long year; for the team before, during and after the trip; for the early work of earthmoving and surveying; and for the friendship between the people of Samasodu and Wamberal CRC.

news.title: Pirini Ponders: June 2018
news.summary: Visiting teams, a laundry for Bethesda, Sol Dolls in Tasmania and new staff settling in.
paragraphs: Greetings from the Solomon Islands. Winter here is much like summer, just with less rain and hotter temperatures.

The base has been busy with visiting teams through May and June, including return visitors working on a secondary school at Samasodu in Isabel. We visited the hospital and hospital school to meet students and learn about resource needs, which CRCA Cadets and GEMS are fundraising for.
Our new administrator and builder are working out very well and have taken on some of the workload.

Base staff have been building a laundry at Bethesda Disability Centre, to be finished before the next intake of students. Ron has been clearing a container of donated goods for the community, doing car repairs and importing a vehicle from Japan.

In late May we spent a couple of weeks in Australia. Tanya spoke at Kingston church in Tasmania and thanked them in person for building our house and supporting our prison ministry. We also helped the ladies of Bethesda sell their Sol Dolls, handmade Solomon Islands dolls, with funds going back to Bethesda to upgrade its facilities.

It has also been a hard couple of months. A good friend from the base was seriously injured in a motorbike accident and was evacuated to Australia for treatment. Within our own family there are health concerns.

Prayer: for our families in New Zealand; for our fathers and decisions about their care; for the CRCA and SIW board as they review the decisions of the last Synod about the direction of the SWIM base; and praise for a good break with family.
All our love and God's blessings, Ron and Tanya

news.title: Pirini Ponders: April 2018
news.summary: Hosting the Ola Fou leadership program and a Bethlehem College team, vehicle repairs and new staff.
paragraphs: Warm greetings from the Solomon Islands. This morning we woke to island music and a language we didn't understand coming from the transit house. It reminded us how much life has changed since we said goodbye to friends and family a year ago.
This week we are hosting 53 people from the Ola Fou Program, an education program that trains young Pacific leaders and youth workers from around the South Pacific and the Solomon Islands.

We are also farewelling a team from Bethlehem College in Tauranga, who worked at Su'u school on Malaita. The students shared how the love and generosity of Solomon Islanders affected them. It was a life-changing experience, and we were glad to support them with logistics.

Ron has been busy with vehicle maintenance, including a clutch replacement on the Hilux with no hoist or workshop, just two tree stumps and blocks of wood. Our new administrator, Rose, and builder, Chris, started in March and are already a blessing. The base has had staff housing and office renovations, and the workshop has been moved.
Tanya has been handing over administration to Rose and continuing with finances and policy work from the board's review. We were thankful for pastoral visits and training from CRCA leaders.

Over Easter we stayed at a lodge an hour from Honiara and hiked through jungle and river crossings to some amazing waterfalls. A quote by Tanya's computer reads, "The will of God will not take us where the grace of God cannot sustain us."

Prayer: for the CRCA Synod in early May and clarity about the direction of the SWIM base; for strength in the heat and the busy season of bookings; for our families in New Zealand; and for safe travel to Australia.
Love and blessings from us to you all, Ron and Tanya

news.title: Pirini Ponders: February 2018
news.summary: School sponsorship fees, base renovations, and medical supplies delivered to Honiara Hospital.
paragraphs: Greetings for 2018. We are back at SWIM after three weeks in New Zealand visiting family, friends, churches and supporters, where we spoke at several churches and morning teas about SWIM's work.

Since returning we have missed the cyclones that hit other islands, and had little rain for the wet season. The base has been very busy with the school sponsorship program, as parents and students come to collect fees for the new semester. Thank you to the donors who make this possible.
Ron has been getting vehicles back on the road with parts brought from New Zealand, and has started renovations to some base properties.

Two board members came back with us. We delivered medical supplies to Honiara Hospital and visited the children's ward and newborn special care unit. We also visited the Hospital School, which SWIM built, and will renew our working relationship with it. Our board chair visited the following week and helped with interviews, and a new office administrator will start soon.

Prayer: for the SIW board and SWIM management as they seek clarity about the direction of the base and staffing; for Tanya's health; for new staff settling in and for staff who have moved on; and for our families in New Zealand.
Love and blessings from us to you all, Ron and Tanya

needsChecking: What SWIM stands for: the owner chose 'Supporting Work in Mission', which the newer newsletters use (the third quarter 2024 bulletin and the 2026 newsletter). The About page and the mission/values PDF on swim.crca.org.au say 'Supporting Work in Ministry', and the third quarter 2024 bulletin's heading also says 'Supporting Workers in Mission'. CLAUDE.md says 'Solomon Islands Work & Instruction in Mission' and should probably be corrected. The page 'name' was left as 'Solomon Islands SWIM'.

Donations: swim.crca.org.au gives no bank account or donation instructions (school sponsorship only says 'your donation will help'). The 2018 newsletter's donation link pointed to the CRCA website and was removed. Bank or giving details need to be supplied if SWIM wants a giving section.

Team list is built from the 2024 to 2026 newsletters, not from the Our Team page (which only shows a Base Manager vacancy from June 2024, now filled). Confirm current staff, roles and spellings (for example 'Mattew Tarai' as printed, 'Phillistus Wate', 'Martina Gegeu') and whether staff are happy to be named. Only Pastor Michael Light has a photo; it is small (about 360px) and comes from the third quarter 2024 bulletin.
Who the SIW Chairperson is: the contact email (repeet777@...) suggests Rod Peet, who leads the Katova teams, but no page says so, so no name is given.

Deed Missionary and Base Manager vacancies: the old site listed both as 'Position vacant'. They are described in 'Full-time roles' without saying they are open. The June 2024 Base Manager vacancy post was not migrated as news because the role was filled in February 2025.

Newsletter news dates are approximate: the quarterly PDFs are dated to the last day of their quarter, and the Pirini Ponders posts that were back-posted on 2019-03-02 (February 2018 to February 2019) and August 2019 (posted November 2019) use the first day of the month in their title. The 'third quarter 2024' bulletin is stored in WordPress with a 2022 date and slug 'swim-news-mid-year-2022-update'; dated 2024-09-30 here.

Personal content: the November 2018 and August 2018 Pirini Ponders letters described family surgery and diagnoses, so they were left out. The remaining 2018–2019 letters mention health only in passing; consider whether to keep them.

Skipped posts: six posts (May 2017, June 2017, July and August 2017, June 2018, July 2018) only linked to PDFs on the old Joomla site (index.php?option=com_edocman...), which no longer exist, so there was nothing to migrate. The PDF links in the Pirini Ponders posts also point to that old Joomla system.
School sponsorship figures from swim.crca.org.au (under 50% primary attendance, 30% secondary enrolment, 18% literacy) are left out because their date and source are not given.

Samasodu history: the mission opportunities page says 'over twelve years', '160 team members' and '7 projects'; the 2018 newsletter says the partnership began in 2006 with '9 trips' and 'over 220 people'. The page uses the 2006 start and avoids the conflicting totals.
Days for Girls: the old site lists it as a ministry area with a photo but gives no detail, so the section is brief.

Video title: the Katova video ID and title come only from swim.json. The newsletters call the school 'Katova High School' or 'Katova Community High School', not 'Katova District High School'. The extra 2018 video (2UGfMUGwWkA) comes from the September 2018 newsletter post.
Facebook links (facebook.com/swimsolomons and the Samasodu mission trips page): only in swim.json; the Samasodu page is also linked from swim.crca.org.au.
'CRCA code of best practice for short-term missions' points to /for-churches?q=missions, copied from SwimPage.tsx. The crca.org.au page links a download, but its PDF URL isn't in the data.
The short-term mission policy PDF tells team leaders to read a 'Long Term / Short Term Missions' document 'on the SWIM website resource page'. That document was not found on swim.crca.org.au.
Hero image: a coastal photo taken from the background of the mission/values PDF. The exact location is not stated, so the alt text does not name a place.

Several photos come from the newsletters and the 2024 bulletin; some are below 800px wide (gallery 01, 04 to 08, and several news images) because no larger versions exist. Some 2024 to 2025 newsletter photos are marked as copyright of the Katova High School Facebook page or Island Sun; none of those were used.
